water_harvesting_conservation__asset_thr.mechanism: Drought impairs these works mainly by exhausting storage or suppressing their benefits rather than by physical damage: subsurface dams in semi-arid Brazil tended to dry out in a rainless year and small ones do not withstand long droughts, and domestic cisterns run out in great multi-year droughts so households fall back on water trucks [ev_drought_hazard_cirilo03_2, ev_drought_hazard_cirilo03_3, ev_drought_hazard_arsky20_3]. In Tunisia, consecutive drought years limited soil-conservation benefits and cut the works established in Medenine to 15 against a target of 95 [ev_drought_hazard_iegtun13_1, ev_drought_hazard_iegtun13_2].
water_harvesting_conservation__asset_thr.conditionality: Only the Tunisian shortfall is an establishment-phase loss of works; the other units describe storage running dry or benefits shrinking, and none quantifies structural damage [ev_drought_hazard_iegtun13_2]. The Brazilian evidence comes from interviews and field observation, and the Tunisian evidence from an ex-post review of project completion data [ev_drought_hazard_arsky20_3, ev_drought_hazard_cirilo03_3, ev_drought_hazard_iegtun13_1].

water_harvesting_conservation__asset_thr.mechanism: Storms cause extensive damage to terraces on China's Loess Plateau, and there are few local funds to repair it [ev_climate_shock_iegchn07_7].
water_harvesting_conservation__asset_thr.conditionality: This is one evaluator observation with no measure of the damage; it adds that farmers' incentive to maintain terraces at their own expense may be undermined by subsidies in adjacent areas, so the threat turns as much on repair finance as on exposure [ev_climate_shock_iegchn07_7].

water_harvesting_conservation__asset_thr.mechanism: Intense runoff overwhelms or breaks structures: floods washed away scores of small dams in northern Ghana, 37.9% of boulder-faced log check dams in Ethiopia failed after a high-magnitude runoff event, check-dam failure releases stored sediment, and large floods could wash out traditional spate diversions in Yemen [ev_flood_damage_veno12_1, ev_check_dam_failure_fran21_2, ev_check_dam_failure_fran21_1, ev_flood_hazard_yem12_3]. On slopes, banquettes lack capacity for erosive rains and overflow, diversion channels fill with eroded soil and overflow in the heaviest storms, and torrential rain collapses terrace walls or carries small terraces away in mass movements [ev_flood_hazard_heusch95_2, ev_flood_hazard_roose94_2, ev_erosion_hazard_willem21_3, ev_erosion_hazard_roose06_5].
water_harvesting_conservation__asset_thr.conditionality: Failure is tied to maintenance and design: rarely maintained diversion systems generally fail after 4 to 10 years, terrace collapse is linked to abandonment, and the Rwandan mass movement happened on steep terraces without trees [ev_flood_hazard_roose94_2, ev_erosion_hazard_willem21_3, ev_erosion_hazard_roose06_5]. Several hazards are extreme-rainfall or landslide events mapped to flood, the sediment-release statement comes from a USA study, and the Yemen statement refers to diversions before project improvements [ev_erosion_hazard_roose06_5, ev_check_dam_failure_fran21_1, ev_flood_hazard_yem12_3].

water_harvesting_conservation__asset_thr.mechanism: Reservoirs, tanks and dams trap the sediment that runoff carries, so storage fills and function declines: Tigray dams with a 30-year design life were set to run their cycle in 4.4 to 5.7 years, eight of ten Zambian reservoirs lost storage to siltation, 31 percent of earthen dams in Haryana silted up within five years, and Moroccan gabions had nearly lost their original function [ev_asset_siltation_saru19_1, ev_asset_siltation_saru19_4, ev_erosion_hazard_iegind11_12, ev_erosion_hazard_iegmar09_2]. Sedimentation is described as perhaps the primary reason for sand dam failure, and tanks desilted in an Indian programme need desilting again within its lifetime [ev_asset_failure_ritc21_3, ev_asset_siltation_verm19_1].
water_harvesting_conservation__asset_thr.conditionality: Severity varies: a Kenyan sand-dam assessment estimates siltation cut storage by 10-25% and judges it neither an inherent limitation nor the main reason dams go unused [ev_asset_siltation_neuf17_1]. Most units are review citations or narrative observations without a common metric, and losses depend on upkeep, as the Moroccan structures failed where no maintenance system had been put in place [ev_asset_siltation_saru19_2, ev_erosion_hazard_iegmar09_2].

water_harvesting_conservation__biodivers.mechanism: Zai planting pits on bare, crusted land trap seed, water and organic matter, so herbaceous and woody species re-establish around the pits within a couple of years; small reservoirs are perceived by users to bring greener surroundings and more biodiversity.
water_harvesting_conservation__biodivers.conditionality: All evidence is narrative species counts or user perceptions from Burkina Faso and Ghana, with no comparison against untreated land and no biodiversity metric; two of the zai units restate the same earlier field observation, so the independent base is thinner than the unit count suggests.

water_harvesting_conservation__carbon_se.mechanism: Water harvesting pits and infiltration trenches are linked to carbon through soil organic matter: zai fields treated for several years showed higher organic matter and nitrogen, and trenches combined with vegetation raised soil nutrients including soil organic carbon.
water_harvesting_conservation__carbon_se.conditionality: Carbon is inferred from a soil organic matter / soil organic carbon proxy, not measured sequestration. The pool is split: trenches in Mexico reduced soil nitrogen and carbon, and a zai trial in Burkina Faso found no significant change in organic matter after two years, so effects appear slow and site-dependent.

water_harvesting_conservation__carbon_se.mechanism: In low-income settings the pathway is zai pits building soil organic matter over time, with organic matter and nitrogen higher on fields treated for several years.
water_harvesting_conservation__carbon_se.conditionality: Both units are zai in Burkina Faso and measure soil organic matter, a proxy for carbon; one is a secondary citation of an earlier study and the other, a controlled trial, found no significant change in organic matter after two years.

water_harvesting_conservation__cost_per_.mechanism: Pooled costs are the up-front works cost per hectare: treatment of sub-watersheds with soil and water conservation works in two India watershed projects, average investment cost of spate-irrigation systems in Yemen (of which farmers paid a share), and rehabilitation of pre-Columbian terraces (andenes) in Peru.
water_harvesting_conservation__cost_per_.conditionality: The pool mixes different denominators and practices: watershed treatment cost per treated hectare in India (lender-evaluation figures), the per-hectare investment cost of spate irrigation systems in Yemen from a completion-report beneficiary survey, and a historical rehabilitation cost for Andean terraces in Peru, an upper-middle-income case. Currency years are not stated for most figures, and the India costs are described by the evaluator as high by national norms.

water_harvesting_conservation__cost_redu.mechanism: Pooled units describe how siting and implementer affect what structures cost: in Karnataka, land-resource-inventory planning avoided unnecessary structures and lowered the construction cost of soil and water conservation works per hectare versus a conventional programme; in Ghana, the share of small dams rehabilitated below given per-irrigated-hectare cost thresholds differed between government and donor/NGO implementers.
water_harvesting_conservation__cost_redu.conditionality: Both are from lower-middle-income countries but measure different things: the India figure is an absolute construction cost per hectare from a lender completion report (the saving is relative to another SWC programme, not to no intervention), and the Ghana figure is a distribution of dam rehabilitation costs by implementer, not a cost reduction.

water_harvesting_conservation__drought__.mechanism: Two routes run through the pooled evidence. In-field practices (zaï and tassa pits, stone bunds, terraces, tied furrows, deep ploughing and residue mulch) let more rain infiltrate and raise soil water, so crops suffer less during dry spells and still yield in dry years: zaï gave 300–400 kg of sorghum in a low-rainfall year on degraded land that otherwise yielded nothing, only tassa fields produced a harvest in the 1990 drought in Niger, and stone-bund plots could yield two to three times more than controls in dry years [ev_soil_water_retention_kabo04_1, ev_soil_water_retention_zoug14_1, ev_drought_hazard_roose93_1, ev_soil_water_retention_brito07_9, ev_soil_water_retention_willem21_1, ev_crop_yield_kabo04_1_s, ev_crop_yield_kabo04_6_s, ev_crop_yield_zoug14_1_s]. Storage structures (domestic and production cisterns, sand dams, subsurface dams and runoff ponds) carry water into the dry season for households, livestock and supplemental irrigation and reduce reliance on water trucks or tankers, and programme evaluations in Ethiopia, Rwanda and China credit watershed works with better drought resilience [ev_water_access_deficit_arsky20_4, ev_water_access_deficit_brito07_1, ev_drought_hazard_castro22_2, ev_water_access_deficit_cirilo03_1, ev_water_access_deficit_ritc21_1, ev_drought_hazard_brito07_10, ev_water_access_deficit_verm19_1, ev_drought_hazard_arega24_4, ev_drought_hazard_rwa18_6, ev_drought_hazard_iegchn07_4].
water_harvesting_conservation__drought__.conditionality: The benefit has limits in severe drought: stone bunds in Burkina Faso gave no yield gain in the driest year and so did not reduce famine risk in a particularly dry year, Niger families practising soil and water conservation still ran an estimated 28 percent deficit in low-rainfall years, and zaï buffers a dry spell of two to three weeks only where soil water storage reaches at least 50 mm [ev_crop_yield_roose94_2, ev_food_security_kabo04_1, ev_drought_hazard_roose93_1]. Storage is also bounded: a 16 thousand-litre cistern gives a family of four 16.6 litres per person-day, at least 67% of 30 Kenyan sand dams could not supply one household through the whole dry season, and no significant soil-moisture effect was found for infiltration trenches or for the Ethiopian CBINReMP watersheds [ev_water_access_deficit_arsky20_2, ev_water_access_deficit_ritc21_3, ev_soil_water_retention_locat20_1, ev_soil_water_retention_abate21_5]. Most units measure soil moisture or household water access as component proxies, the largest yield contrasts are cited figures or author assertions, and several results are bundled programmes or Bank, Embrapa and implementer self-assessments in which the water-harvesting share is not isolated [ev_crop_yield_kabo04_1_s, ev_crop_yield_zoug14_1_s, ev_drought_hazard_rwa18_6, ev_soil_water_retention_kar20_2, ev_water_access_deficit_silva09_2].

water_harvesting_conservation__drought__.mechanism: The evidence here is mostly from semi-arid Brazil: domestic and production cisterns, runoff ponds used for supplemental irrigation and subsurface dams store rain into the dry season, giving households basic drinking water, keeping livestock watered when clay tanks are dry, reducing reliance on water trucks and reducing crop-loss risk in irregular years [ev_water_access_deficit_arsky20_1, ev_water_access_deficit_arsky20_5, ev_water_access_deficit_arsky20_4, ev_water_access_deficit_cirilo03_1, ev_drought_hazard_brito07_10, ev_drought_hazard_castro22_2]. In-field tillage (deep ploughing, tied furrows) and terraces raise soil moisture, with broad bench terraces in semi-arid China holding up to 22% more moisture than vegetated slopes [ev_soil_water_retention_brito07_9, ev_soil_water_retention_willem21_1, ev_soil_water_retention_willem21_2].
water_harvesting_conservation__drought__.conditionality: Storage caps the benefit: a 16 thousand-litre cistern gives a family of four 16.6 litres per person-day, larger households stay dependent on water trucks, and only 19.1% of surveyed families used the cistern as their main source [ev_water_access_deficit_arsky20_2, ev_water_access_deficit_brito07_1, ev_water_access_deficit_silva09_2]. Much of the pool is implementer, Embrapa or agency assessment, interviews, or census inference without a counterfactual, and the units measure water access or soil moisture as component proxies rather than drought losses [ev_water_access_deficit_castro22_1, ev_water_access_deficit_arsky20_4, ev_soil_water_retention_brito07_9]. A review of infiltration trenches found no significant soil-moisture effect, and the evidence comes from upper-middle-income settings [ev_soil_water_retention_locat20_1].

water_harvesting_conservation__drought_h.mechanism: Stored or infiltrated water buffers dry periods: zai pits hold soil water so crops survive short dry spells, cisterns and runoff ponds supply supplemental irrigation and livestock water during droughts, and watershed works raise water availability so households and watersheds cope better with drought.
water_harvesting_conservation__drought_h.conditionality: Most units are narrative or expert assertions (Embrapa and cistern-programme authors in Brazil, a lender review in China) with no drought metric; the strongest is an independent DIME evaluation in Rwanda reported through a completion report, and an Ethiopian public-works study notes vegetation still tracks local drought severity. The zai effect is conditional on enough soil water storage capacity.

water_harvesting_conservation__establish.mechanism: Establishment costs pooled here are the up-front costs of building or rehabilitating structures: soil and water conservation treatments per hectare in two India watershed projects, average investment cost per hectare of spate-irrigation systems in Yemen (with the farmer's share), and rehabilitation of Andean terraces in Peru.
water_harvesting_conservation__establish.conditionality: The pool mixes different denominators and practices: watershed treatment cost per treated hectare in India (lender-evaluation figures), the per-hectare investment cost of spate irrigation systems in Yemen from a completion-report beneficiary survey, and a historical rehabilitation cost for Andean terraces in Peru, an upper-middle-income case. Currency years are not stated for most figures, and the India costs are described by the evaluator as high by national norms.

water_harvesting_conservation__fire__all.mechanism: The source reasons that on intensively tended terraces, where all crop residues are grazed off as soon as harvests end, fire finds no fuel, so terraces can act as a firebreak [ev_fire_hazard_roose06_1].
water_harvesting_conservation__fire__all.conditionality: This is an expert estimate that the authors state has no experimental basis on terraces, and it depends on residues being removed by grazing; grass strips may instead carry fire if they are not grazed [ev_fire_hazard_roose06_1].

water_harvesting_conservation__flood__al.mechanism: Contour stone bunds, bench and progressive terraces, banquettes and infiltration trenches slow and spread runoff on hillslopes: terraces cut mean runoff by 50 to 98% and flood peaks on small mountain plots, stone bunds lower peak discharges and roughly halve sediment transport, trenches cut plot runoff by 46.4% on average, and in a semi-arid Tunisian catchment a combined treatment lengthened flood rise time, doubled base time and cut runoff volume by 50% [ev_runoff_reduction_roose06_1, ev_flood_hazard_roose06_1, ev_erosion_hazard_roose94_1, ev_runoff_reduction_locat20_1, ev_runoff_reduction_roose06_2]. Retention-walled hill terraces in Uttarakhand, spate structures in Yemen and small reservoirs in northern Ghana are also credited with limiting flood impacts [ev_flood_hazard_utk22_7, ev_flood_hazard_yem12_4, ev_flood_hazard_veno12_1].
water_harvesting_conservation__flood__al.conditionality: Most units are runoff or soil-loss measurements standing in for flood impact at plot or small-catchment scale; catchment-level terrace evidence is scarce, an Uttarakhand water-budget model showed overall surface runoff up 1.5 percent, and Karnataka project watersheds cut runoff by only 3.2 percent against conventional sites [ev_flood_hazard_willem21_1, ev_runoff_reduction_utk22_4, ev_runoff_reduction_kar20_1]. Diversion structures work the other way: diversion banquettes in Niger doubled the runoff coefficient and raised peak discharges, diversion systems accelerate concentration time, larger sand dams increase flooding risk, and check dams can cause downstream channel incision [ev_runoff_reduction_heusch95_1, ev_flood_hazard_heusch95_1, ev_flood_hazard_roose94_3, ev_flood_hazard_ritc21_1, ev_erosion_hazard_fran21_1]. The Uttarakhand, Yemen and Ethiopian statements are Bank self-evaluations or perception surveys, the Ghana finding is user perception, and the Tunisian result bundles rangeland closure and gully stone-filling with the bunds [ev_flood_hazard_utk22_7, ev_flood_hazard_yem12_4, ev_runoff_reduction_eth16_2, ev_flood_hazard_veno12_1, ev_runoff_reduction_roose06_2].

water_harvesting_conservation__flood_haz.mechanism: Terraces, contour stone bunds and spate or diversion structures slow and spread runoff, lowering peak discharges and lengthening flood rise times; in a semi-arid Tunisian catchment a combined treatment clipped peak discharges, doubled base time and cut the runoff volume of 71 single-peak floods by 50%, and small reservoirs are perceived by users to limit rainy-season floods [ev_flood_hazard_roose06_1, ev_flood_hazard_roose94_1, ev_flood_hazard_roose06_2_s, ev_flood_hazard_veno12_1].
water_harvesting_conservation__flood_haz.conditionality: Direction depends on design: diversion banquettes in Niger and runoff-diversion dikes increased peak flows, dike failure risks gullying, and larger sand dams increase flooding risk [ev_flood_hazard_heusch95_1, ev_flood_hazard_roose94_3, ev_flood_hazard_ritc21_1]. Catchment-scale evidence is scarce, with a review calling the terrace effect on peak flow uncertain, the Tunisian result bundles rangeland closure and gully stone-filling with the bunds, and the Yemen and Uttarakhand statements are lender self-reported assertions without measurement [ev_flood_hazard_willem21_1, ev_flood_hazard_roose06_2_s, ev_flood_hazard_yem12_4, ev_flood_hazard_utk22_7].

water_harvesting_conservation__heat_stre.mechanism: A review of quasi-experimental studies reports that the impact of soil and water conservation is especially significant in areas with temperature shocks or lower rainfall [ev_crop_yield_mala24_5].
water_harvesting_conservation__heat_stre.conditionality: This is one narrative statement from a review that does not name specific practices, does not separate heat shocks from low rainfall and gives no magnitude; no unit measures heat-stress losses directly [ev_crop_yield_mala24_5].

water_harvesting_conservation__productio.mechanism: Water harvesting and conservation structures capture runoff and raise soil moisture in the root zone, so rainfed crops yield more, especially in dry years and low-rainfall areas; stored water also enables supplemental irrigation, extra crop cycles and diversification, zaï and stone lines trap sediment, manure and organic matter, and terracing levels slopes to retain moisture. In Burkina Faso stone bunds raised sorghum yields by 33% to 55%, and by about 142% with compost, while in drought years zaï and tassa fields produced a harvest where untreated land gave little or none [ev_crop_yield_zoug14_2, ev_crop_yield_zoug14_4, ev_crop_yield_kabo04_1_s, ev_crop_yield_kabo04_6_s].
water_harvesting_conservation__productio.conditionality: The pool mixes independent evaluations (IFPRI/ESSP matching studies in Ethiopia, a DIME difference-in-difference in Rwanda) with lender self-reported completion-report figures and bundled watershed programmes in which SWC works came with seed, fertiliser and crop packages, so the share attributable to the structures is unclear. Null or negative results are present: SWC promoted mostly off-farm had no yield effect, late adopters and the pooled sample in Ethiopia showed no significant gain, bunds lowered yields in high-rainfall Amhara, zaï lowered sorghum yields under waterlogging in humid Cameroon, and diversion banquettes in Niger cut yields. Zaï pits alone gave an average sorghum gain of only 38 kg/ha in one study against 310 kg/ha in another, so much of the benefit rides on the manure or compost added, and benefits can take several years of maintained structures to appear [ev_crop_yield_kabo04_2, ev_crop_yield_kabo04_3].

water_harvesting_conservation__productio.mechanism: In semi-arid settings, pits (zai, tassa), stone bunds, tied furrows and subsurface dams concentrate scarce rainfall in the root zone or store it for later use, raising cereal yields and enabling harvests in drought years when untreated fields fail.
water_harvesting_conservation__productio.conditionality: Evidence mixes Sahelian field results (Burkina Faso, Niger) with Embrapa and cistern-programme sources from semi-arid Brazil, several of them self-assessments or expert statements; the Brazilian programme effects are on value of production, a proxy, and some yield gains depend on manure added to the pits.

water_harvesting_conservation__productio.mechanism: In rainfed hill and watershed systems, in-situ rainwater conservation, terracing and soil and water conservation works combined with crop packages raise yields: average rainfed crop yields rose 24% and 26% against controls in Karnataka watershed phases, rainfed crop productivity rose 20.8 percent by difference-in-difference in Uttarakhand, and maize on terraced Rwandan hillsides rose from 1.5 to 2.8 tons per hectare [ev_crop_yield_iegind11_1, ev_crop_yield_utk22_1, ev_crop_yield_rwa18_7]. The DIME evaluation reported for Rwanda found the value of harvests 36 percent higher than in the control group [ev_agricultural_production_value_rwa18_3].
water_harvesting_conservation__productio.conditionality: Every unit is a bundled programme in which conservation works came with improved seed, vermicompost, crop packages or life-saving irrigation, so the share due to water harvesting is not isolated, and all are drawn from Bank completion reports or IEG reviews of them [ev_crop_yield_hp17_2, ev_crop_yield_utk22_8, ev_crop_yield_iegind11_1]. The Rwanda maize figure is project monitoring before and after without a control, and the Uttarakhand terrace figure compares with- and without-project models [ev_crop_yield_rwa18_7, ev_crop_yield_utk22_8].

water_harvesting_conservation__productio.mechanism: In the Brazilian semi-arid, subsurface dams, tied furrows, micro-catchments with rescue irrigation and production cisterns store or concentrate water, raising crop productivity, enabling extra harvests and expanding the value of family production; in the Andes, infiltration trenches raised yields on some plots.
water_harvesting_conservation__productio.conditionality: Upper-middle-income evidence only, largely Embrapa and programme self-assessments plus one quasi-experimental study of value of production (a proxy); a trench review from Peru reports both positive and negative yield effects, and one cistern-programme author states there are no quantitative impact evaluations.

water_harvesting_conservation__rural_pov.mechanism: Higher and more stable yields, irrigation of gardens and higher-value crops from stored water, and livestock watering raise household income and food security; beneficiaries shift from staples to vegetables, and returns per hectare or per unit of labour can exceed alternatives. A quasi-experimental study cited in a review found soil and water conservation raised net rice profit in Ghana by a significant 16 per cent [ev_economic_return_mala24_1].
water_harvesting_conservation__rural_pov.conditionality: Much of the income evidence comes from bundled watershed programmes and lender completion reports (India, China, Yemen, Mauritania, Rwanda), where evaluators flag weak attribution, one-off wages from construction, or returns driven by subsidies rather than productivity. Independent evaluations are more cautious: no significant effect on food security or total income in Ethiopian programmes, terraces reducing net crop income, a Brazilian cistern programme with a benefit-cost ratio well below one, single SWC measures not covering their annual costs, and sand dams likely not cost-efficient. Food-security and income figures are proxies for poverty.

water_harvesting_conservation__rural_pov.mechanism: In semi-arid areas, cisterns and subsurface dams let families irrigate gardens and fruit, diversifying diets and raising farm income, while zai and stone bunds raise cereal output and return to labour; food security rises with the area of farm under bunds.
water_harvesting_conservation__rural_pov.conditionality: Income gains from the Brazilian cistern programme are small and turned negative for larger farms, its benefit-cost ratio is well below one, and subsurface dams yielded little cash income in stagnant local economies; a Sahelian study found SWC families still in deficit in low-rainfall years, and single SWC measures did not repay annual costs.

water_harvesting_conservation__rural_pov.mechanism: In the Brazilian semi-arid, cisterns and subsurface dams supply water for gardens, fruit and livestock, improving diets and raising family farm income, with the largest income effects on small farms; Andean terrace rehabilitation is judged to pay back through long durability.
water_harvesting_conservation__rural_pov.conditionality: Evidence is from upper-middle-income Brazil and Peru, outside the LIC/LMIC target band. A quasi-experimental study found modest income gains, no effect outside the Northeast, a negative effect on larger farms and a benefit-cost ratio far below one; several units are Embrapa or programme self-assessments and household self-reports.

water_harvesting_conservation__soil_eros.mechanism: Terraces, stone bunds, banquettes, trenches and check dams slow overland flow and spread it behind barriers, so less runoff leaves the slope and less soil is detached and carried away; check dams and gabions trap sediment in channels. Measured reductions are large: terraces cut soil losses on small mountain plots from more than 200 to under 2 t/ha a year, Burundi terrace plots cut erosion by 50% to 90%, trenches reduced soil loss by 73.0% on average, and check dams cut catchment sediment export by 20 to 98% [ev_erosion_hazard_roose06_1_s, ev_erosion_hazard_roose06_2_s, ev_erosion_hazard_locat20_1, ev_sediment_retention_fran21_1].
water_harvesting_conservation__soil_eros.conditionality: Most plot-scale measurements and syntheses agree, but several sources are lender self-reports with before/after designs, perception surveys or catchment numbers that barely changed: the Rwanda sediment drop from 54 to 2.6 tons/ha a year has no control, and Uttarakhand sediment yield moved only from 71.6 to 69.3 tons per ha per year [ev_erosion_hazard_rwa18_1_s, ev_erosion_hazard_utk22_3, ev_erosion_hazard_yem12_5]; runoff reduction is used as a component proxy. Negative findings: check dams can cause downstream channel incision, diversion banquettes increased gully and bank erosion in Niger, trenches raised sediment in the first years, Maghreb banquettes were often erased or unmaintained, and abandoned terraces increase erosion [ev_erosion_hazard_fran21_1, ev_erosion_hazard_heusch95_1, ev_erosion_hazard_locat20_2, ev_erosion_hazard_roose06_4, ev_erosion_hazard_willem21_2].

water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.mechanism: In Tunisia, consecutive drought years reduced agricultural and pastoral productivity gains and limited soil-conservation benefits, and drought cut the spate-irrigation and water-recharge works established in Medenine to 15 against a target of 95 [ev_drought_hazard_iegtun13_1, ev_drought_hazard_iegtun13_2].
water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.conditionality: Both units come from one ex-post review drawing on project completion data; one describes an establishment-phase shortfall and the other a reduced benefit, not physical damage to built works [ev_drought_hazard_iegtun13_2, ev_drought_hazard_iegtun13_1].

water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.mechanism: Costs are the per-hectare unit cost of watershed treatments (bunds, check dams and other soil and water conservation works) across treated area in two World Bank-supported India watershed projects.
water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.conditionality: Both figures come from one evaluation of bundled watershed programmes in India and are treatment costs per hectare treated, not per hectare of degraded land restored; the evaluator compares them with national budget norms rather than with outcomes.

water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.mechanism: Better-sited planning based on a land resource inventory avoided unnecessary structures, so construction of soil and water conservation works cost less per hectare than under the conventional integrated watershed programme.
water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.conditionality: Single lender completion-report figure from Karnataka, India, in local currency at stated price terms; the comparison is against another watershed programme, so it shows a saving from planning rather than the cost of SWC versus no SWC.

water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.mechanism: These are programme-scale packages of soil and water conservation and water-harvesting works. In India, participating villages cut tanker water transport by 56 percent against non-participating villages and Karnataka project watersheds had soil moisture 30.5 percent higher than conventional watershed sites; in Ethiopia the PSNP public works raised water availability and watershed drought resilience, and in semi-arid Brazil cisterns expanded rural water access and can reduce animal mortality in severe drought [ev_water_access_deficit_verm19_1, ev_soil_water_retention_kar20_2, ev_drought_hazard_arega24_4, ev_water_access_deficit_castro22_1, ev_drought_hazard_castro22_2]. A review of quasi-experimental studies finds soil and water conservation methods particularly useful in regions with low rainfall or high climatic variability [ev_crop_yield_mala24_3].
water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.conditionality: Every unit is a bundled programme or unspecified soil and water conservation, so the share due to water harvesting is not isolated; the Karnataka figure comes from a Bank completion report, and the Brazilian statements are a census-based inference without a counterfactual and a statement of potential [ev_soil_water_retention_kar20_2, ev_water_access_deficit_castro22_1, ev_drought_hazard_castro22_2]. An independent Ethiopian evaluation found no significant difference in remote-sensed soil water retention between beneficiary and control watersheds, the PSNP note adds that vegetation greenness still followed local drought severity, and Niger families with soil and water conservation still had an estimated 28 percent deficit in low-rainfall years [ev_soil_water_retention_abate21_5, ev_drought_hazard_arega24_4, ev_food_security_kabo04_1].

water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.mechanism: Watershed works and production cisterns increase stored water, which improves watershed drought resilience and can reduce livestock deaths in severe droughts.
water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.conditionality: One Ethiopian public-works study (bundled area closures, small-scale irrigation and SWC) and one Brazilian cistern-programme expert statement framed as a potential effect; neither quantifies drought impacts.

water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.mechanism: Watershed programmes combining physical and vegetative barriers, bunds, check dams and terraces reduce runoff and soil loss: runoff dropped by 5 to 18 percent across Indian states, downstream runoff in the Karnataka catchments examined fell by 10 to 22 percent, and Ethiopian public works cut soil loss by 32.2% [ev_runoff_reduction_iegind11_6, ev_runoff_reduction_iegind11_5, ev_erosion_hazard_eth16_4, ev_erosion_hazard_arega24_3].
water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.conditionality: All units are bundled programme results measuring runoff or soil loss as proxies for flood impact, several from Bank completion reports or perception surveys, such as 84 percent of Ethiopian respondents reporting reduced run-off [ev_runoff_reduction_eth16_2, ev_erosion_hazard_eth16_4, ev_runoff_reduction_kar20_1]. Effects at watershed scale are small or absent: Karnataka project watersheds cut runoff by 3.2 percent against conventional sites, Uttarakhand sediment yield fell only from 71.6 to 69.3 tons per ha per year, and its water-budget model showed overall surface runoff up 1.5 percent [ev_runoff_reduction_kar20_1, ev_erosion_hazard_utk22_3, ev_runoff_reduction_utk22_4].

water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.mechanism: A review of quasi-experimental studies reports that the impact of soil and water conservation is especially significant in areas with temperature shocks or lower rainfall [ev_crop_yield_mala24_5].
water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.conditionality: This is one narrative statement from a review that does not name specific practices, does not separate heat shocks from low rainfall and gives no magnitude; no unit measures heat-stress losses directly [ev_crop_yield_mala24_5].

water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.mechanism: Soil and water conservation structures (terraces, bunds, check dams) retain moisture and soil, raising crop yields and value of production; the gains are larger in low-rainfall or climatically variable areas and in dry periods. Water harvesting with irrigation also lets households diversify crops.
water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.conditionality: Most magnitudes are from bundled programmes or lender completion reports (Ethiopia public works, India watershed projects, Mauritania), with value-of-production and forage biomass used as proxies. Independent Ethiopian studies show effects only for early adopters and only after several years of maintained structures; SWC promoted off-farm, imposed structures, and bunds in high-rainfall areas showed no gain or losses.

water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.mechanism: Watershed and SWC programmes raise household income through higher yields, irrigation and diversification, and watershed investments in India show modest positive returns across many case studies. A quasi-experimental study cited in a review found soil and water conservation raised net rice profit in Ghana by a significant 16 per cent [ev_economic_return_mala24_1].
water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.conditionality: Most magnitudes are from bundled programmes with weak attribution (IEG calls a China income estimate not robust and notes India income gains may partly be construction wages; a Karnataka ICR doubts its own before/after figures). Independent studies found no effect on food security or per capita income, household benefit-cost ratios mostly below one at market wages in Ethiopia, and a cistern programme benefit-cost ratio well below one in Brazil; income and food-security figures are proxies for poverty.

water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.mechanism: Physical SWC works under public-works and watershed programmes reduce soil loss and downstream runoff, and sediment-control dams with terraces and vegetation trap sediment in the catchment.
water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.conditionality: Nearly all units are programme or lender reports from Ethiopia, India and China, often perception surveys or before/after comparisons; an Uttarakhand water budget showed surface runoff slightly increasing, the Karnataka runoff comparison is against another SWC programme, and IEG doubts the India runoff measurements. Effects mixing runoff and soil-loss metrics are only components of erosion risk.

water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.mechanism: Sediment-control dams, terraces and vegetation in a Loess Plateau watershed programme capture sediment each year, reducing the load reaching downstream rivers.
water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.conditionality: Single modelled programme-level estimate from a lender review in China, using sediment retention as a proxy for water quality.

water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.mechanism: Watershed SWC and recharge structures raise water tables and spring discharge, enabling small-scale irrigation and reducing water transport by tanker in participating villages.
water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.conditionality: Mostly programme reports from India and Ethiopia without untreated comparison sites; IEG notes recharge gains may be wiped out by subsidised tube-well pumping, year-round wells did not increase in Burkina Faso, and the Uttarakhand recharge change is a small modelled water-budget figure.

water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.mechanism: Zai pits concentrate runoff, seed and organic matter on crusted, degraded soils, raising germination and the spread of seed so that herbaceous and woody species recolonise formerly bare fields.
water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.conditionality: Evidence is limited to zai in Burkina Faso and is descriptive (species re-establishing after a few years, revegetation judged very positive), not a measured biodiversity outcome against a control; two units cite the same earlier observation.

water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.mechanism: In-situ structures (zai pits, infiltration trenches) can raise soil organic matter and soil organic carbon by concentrating water and organic inputs, especially when trenches are combined with vegetation.
water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.conditionality: Soil organic carbon is a proxy for sequestration. Evidence is mixed: trenches in Mexico lowered soil nitrogen and carbon, and short zai trials showed no significant soil change; gains come from multi-year zai or vegetated trenches.

water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.mechanism: Zaï and tassa pits, tied furrows, deep ploughing and residue mulch increase infiltration and soil water storage, so crops suffer less from dry spells at the onset of and during the rainy season [ev_soil_water_retention_kabo04_1, ev_soil_water_retention_brito07_9, ev_drought_hazard_roose93_1]. In rainfall-deficit periods zaï allowed cereals to be grown on degraded crusted soils, gave 300–400 kg of sorghum in a low-rainfall year where untreated land yielded nothing, and only tassa fields produced a harvest in the 1990 drought in Niger; with 80% or more residue cover, available soil water can be up to 20% greater than on bare soil [ev_crop_yield_roose93_3, ev_crop_yield_kabo04_1_s, ev_crop_yield_kabo04_6_s, ev_soil_water_retention_fao13c_1].
water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.conditionality: Zaï only reduces the impact of a dry spell of two to three weeks, and only where soil water storage capacity is at least 50 mm, and the mulch manual notes its usefulness falls as the water deficit becomes more severe [ev_drought_hazard_roose93_1, ev_soil_water_retention_fao13c_1]. A review of infiltration trenches found no significant soil-moisture effect because only four studies had usable statistics, and the Brazilian tillage result is a single-season station trial by the institution that promotes the technologies [ev_soil_water_retention_locat20_1, ev_soil_water_retention_brito07_9]. The large zaï and tassa yield contrasts are an author estimate and assertion rather than controlled comparisons [ev_crop_yield_kabo04_1_s, ev_crop_yield_kabo04_6_s].

water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.mechanism: Zai pits concentrate runoff into the root zone, so crops can ride out a dry spell of two to three weeks.
water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.conditionality: Single expert statement from Burkina Faso, explicitly conditional on the soil having sufficient water storage capacity.

water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.mechanism: Infiltration trenches intercept hillslope runoff: across the reviewed mountain studies they cut plot runoff by 46.4% and soil loss by 73.0% on average, and reduced sheet erosion on degraded high-Andean soils [ev_runoff_reduction_locat20_1, ev_erosion_hazard_locat20_1, ev_erosion_hazard_locat20_3].
water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.conditionality: All units come from one review, and the runoff effect was much weaker on cropland (3.5% of rainfall) than on land with natural vegetation (15%) [ev_runoff_reduction_locat20_2, ev_runoff_reduction_locat20_3]. Some studies found catchment sediment concentration rising in the first years after trenches were built, and runoff and soil loss stand in for flood impact rather than measuring flood peaks [ev_erosion_hazard_locat20_2].

water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.mechanism: Planting pits (zaï, tassa), tied furrows and infiltration trenches capture runoff in the root zone; combined with manure they raise cereal yields on degraded crusted soils and allow a harvest in drought years when untreated fields fail. With zaï, sorghum yields ranged from 300–400 kg in a low-rainfall year to 1500 kg/ha in a good year on degraded land that otherwise yielded nothing, and in the 1990 drought in Niger only tassa fields produced a harvest [ev_crop_yield_kabo04_1_s, ev_crop_yield_kabo04_6_s].
water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.conditionality: Much of the yield gain depends on manure or mineral fertiliser added to the pits: pits alone gave an average sorghum gain of only 38 kg/ha over two seasons in one study, against 310 kg/ha in a regression study at Donsin [ev_crop_yield_kabo04_2, ev_crop_yield_kabo04_3]. Zaï lowered sorghum yields under waterlogging in humid Cameroon, trench effects on yield were positive on some plots and negative on others, and the Himachal Pradesh demonstration figure is a lender self-report bundled with improved seed and irrigation; the largest zaï and tassa contrasts are author estimates rather than controlled trials [ev_crop_yield_roose93_4, ev_crop_yield_locat20_2, ev_crop_yield_hp17_2, ev_crop_yield_kabo04_1_s].

water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.mechanism: Zai and stone or earth bunds raise yields enough that returns to labour exceed the local shadow wage and per-hectare net benefits are positive; bunds also show positive financial returns at subproject level.
water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.conditionality: The Burkina Faso figures are secondary model estimates and the Mauritania return is a lender self-reported subproject evaluation; manual zai gives far smaller net benefits than mechanised zai in the same source.

water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.mechanism: Infiltration trenches intercept and infiltrate runoff, cutting plot-level runoff and sheet-erosion soil loss; the runoff reduction is larger on natural vegetation than on cropland.
water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.conditionality: All units come from one review of trenches, largely in the Peruvian Andes (upper-middle income). The same review reports increased catchment sediment in the first years after construction, and plot-level effects may not transfer to catchments.

water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.mechanism: Earth and stone bunds and infiltration trenches are meant to increase infiltration and replenish shallow groundwater, and communities in Mauritania report rising well levels.
water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.conditionality: The Mauritania evidence is a lender-reported community perception bundled with fencing; a trench review found no significant effect on infiltration rates and little effect on baseflow in the Peruvian Andes, and catchment-level recharge gains could not be generalised.

water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.mechanism: In the humid Sudanian zone of Cameroon, where daily rains exceed 80 mm, zaï pits concentrate infiltration, and sorghum in the pits yielded less than flat-cultivated fields because of frequent waterlogging and nutrient leaching [ev_crop_yield_roose93_4].
water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.conditionality: This is one unpublished observation cited by the authors, with no magnitude; it marks zaï as unsuited to high-rainfall sites rather than showing a general effect [ev_crop_yield_roose93_4].

water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.mechanism: In great multi-year droughts the domestic cistern runs dry and households fall back on water trucks, which the source links to political use of water supply [ev_drought_hazard_arsky20_3].
water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.conditionality: This is a functional failure of storage described in an implementer interview from semi-arid Brazil, not structural damage, and it is not quantified [ev_drought_hazard_arsky20_3].

water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.mechanism: Domestic rooftop cisterns in semi-arid Brazil store rainwater for the dry period, giving households basic drinking and cooking water near the home, cutting the time spent fetching water and postponing or avoiding the extreme shortages that used to send families to water trucks [ev_water_access_deficit_arsky20_1, ev_water_access_deficit_silva09_1, ev_water_access_deficit_arsky20_4]. In a survey of beneficiary families, 57.8% said the cistern fully met drinking, cooking and personal hygiene needs [ev_water_access_deficit_silva09_2].
water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.conditionality: The benefit is set by storage per person: a 16 thousand-litre cistern gives a family of four 16.6 litres per person-day, and households of more than five people stay dependent on water trucks [ev_water_access_deficit_arsky20_2, ev_water_access_deficit_brito07_1]. Only 19.1% of surveyed families named the cistern as their main water source, the survey used recall with no control group and was commissioned by the programme funder, and the other units are implementer or author statements [ev_water_access_deficit_silva09_2, ev_water_access_deficit_silva09_1, ev_water_access_deficit_arsky20_1]. The evidence covers domestic water access as a component proxy for drought impact, not crop or livestock losses, and comes only from semi-arid Brazil.

water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.mechanism: The pooled cost is the average construction cost of a roof rainwater-harvesting tank under the Himachal Pradesh mid-Himalayan watershed project in India, reported per structure from the project's output table.
water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.conditionality: A single lender completion report, self-reported from physical and financial monitoring; the figure is a nominal rupee average over the project years converted at one exchange rate, so it indicates the order of cost of a household tank rather than a transferable unit rate.

water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.mechanism: Domestic rooftop cisterns supply drinking and household water rather than productive water, so most beneficiaries report improved quality of life but no change in income.
water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.conditionality: Single Embrapa household survey in semi-arid Brazil (upper-middle income, self-reported); the null concerns cash income, not other welfare outcomes.

water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.mechanism: Domestic rooftop cisterns store rainwater beside the house, giving households basic drinking and cooking water through the dry season, sharply reducing time spent fetching water and dependence on water trucks.
water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.conditionality: All evidence is from cistern programmes in semi-arid Brazil (upper-middle income), largely programme authors and Embrapa surveys. A standard cistern covers basic needs only for small households, larger families remain dependent on water trucks, and most households still use other sources as their main supply.

water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.mechanism: Subsurface dams in semi-arid Brazil tended to dry up during a year without rain, and small manually built dams do not withstand long droughts, limiting production through dry spells [ev_drought_hazard_cirilo03_2, ev_drought_hazard_cirilo03_3].
water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.conditionality: Both units describe storage exhaustion rather than structural damage; one comes from interviews with seven families, the effect depends on dam size, and subsurface dams sit in this family provisionally [ev_drought_hazard_cirilo03_3, ev_drought_hazard_cirilo03_2].

water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.mechanism: Floods washed away scores of small dams in northern Ghana, 37.9% of boulder-faced log check dams in Ethiopia still failed after a high-magnitude runoff event, and when peak flows break check dams the stored sediment is released rapidly [ev_flood_damage_veno12_1, ev_check_dam_failure_fran21_2, ev_check_dam_failure_fran21_1].
water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.conditionality: The check-dam evidence is cited from other studies, and the sediment-release statement comes from a USA study outside the low- and middle-income target [ev_check_dam_failure_fran21_2, ev_check_dam_failure_fran21_1]. The Ghana finding records damage that triggered a rehabilitation programme, without a count of dams lost [ev_flood_damage_veno12_1].

water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.mechanism: Reservoirs, tanks and dams trap the sediment that runoff carries, so storage fills and function declines: Tigray dams with a 30-year design life were set to run their cycle in 4.4 to 5.7 years, eight of ten Zambian reservoirs lost storage to siltation, 31 percent of earthen dams in Haryana silted up within five years, and Moroccan gabions had nearly lost their original function [ev_asset_siltation_saru19_1, ev_asset_siltation_saru19_4, ev_erosion_hazard_iegind11_12, ev_erosion_hazard_iegmar09_2]. Sedimentation is described as perhaps the primary reason for sand dam failure, and tanks desilted in an Indian programme need desilting again within its lifetime [ev_asset_failure_ritc21_3, ev_asset_siltation_verm19_1].
water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.conditionality: Severity varies: a Kenyan sand-dam assessment estimates siltation cut storage by 10-25% and judges it neither an inherent limitation nor the main reason dams go unused [ev_asset_siltation_neuf17_1]. Most units are review citations or narrative observations without a common metric, and losses depend on upkeep, as the Moroccan structures failed where no maintenance system had been put in place [ev_asset_siltation_saru19_2, ev_erosion_hazard_iegmar09_2].

water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.mechanism: Small reservoirs retain water in the landscape, which users associate with greener surroundings and improved biodiversity around the sites.
water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.conditionality: A single user-perception statement from small reservoirs in Ghana; there is no ecological measurement behind it.

water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.mechanism: The unit reports how often rehabilitated small dams in Ghana came in under per-irrigated-hectare cost thresholds, comparing the government irrigation authority with donor and NGO implementers.
water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.conditionality: This is a cost distribution by implementer for reservoir rehabilitation, not a measured cost reduction from water harvesting; treat it as context on rehabilitation cost variability.

water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.mechanism: Runoff-fed storage holds water into the dry season: Kenyan communities with a sand dam had water 2.5 months longer than those relying on the riverbed, subsurface dams in Brazil raised well levels that households used when other sources dried up, production cisterns kept livestock watered while household tanks were dry, and pond water applied as supplemental irrigation during in-season dry spells reduced farming risk [ev_water_access_deficit_ritc21_1, ev_water_access_deficit_cirilo03_1, ev_water_access_deficit_arsky20_5, ev_drought_hazard_brito07_10]. A review of small reservoirs and a Loess Plateau evaluation of runoff cisterns also credit them with drought resilience and with mitigating the effects of frequent droughts [ev_drought_hazard_saru19_1, ev_drought_hazard_iegchn07_4].
water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.conditionality: Storage capacity limits the effect: at least 67% of 30 Kenyan sand dams could not supply even one household through the whole dry season, and 57% of assessed dams would provide four months of water for their reported users only if it were their sole source [ev_water_access_deficit_ritc21_3, ev_water_access_deficit_neuf17_1]. The Loess Plateau drought claim is a qualitative assertion, the reservoir finding is a vote count, and the Brazilian pond statement is an institutional self-assessment without data [ev_drought_hazard_iegchn07_4, ev_drought_hazard_saru19_1, ev_drought_hazard_brito07_10]. Sand dams and subsurface dams are filed in this family provisionally, pending a sub-practice decision.

water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.mechanism: Cisterns and runoff ponds store water that is used as supplemental (rescue) irrigation during in-season dry spells or for households, reducing crop losses in irregular-rainfall years.
water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.conditionality: Evidence is narrative: an Embrapa expert account from semi-arid Brazil, a lender review asserting cisterns in China mitigate drought without measurement, and a review vote count; no drought-loss metric is reported.

water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.mechanism: The pooled costs are average construction costs of village ponds or tanks per structure and of dry-stone drainage-line check dams per cubic metre of structure, from the output table of the Himachal Pradesh mid-Himalayan watershed project in India.
water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.conditionality: One lender completion report, self-reported from project monitoring, in nominal rupees converted at a single exchange rate; the per-cubic-metre figure is per cubic metre of masonry built, not per cubic metre of water stored, so it is not comparable with storage-cost figures and the cost class should be read with that denominator in mind.

water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.mechanism: Small reservoirs store runoff: hill reservoirs in the Merguellil basin in Tunisia were modelled to reduce outlet flows by 13%, and users of small reservoirs in northern Ghana list limiting rainy-season floods among their benefits [ev_runoff_reduction_roose06_4, ev_flood_hazard_veno12_1].
water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.conditionality: The Tunisian figure is modelled and the Ghana finding is user perception, not a measured flood reduction [ev_runoff_reduction_roose06_4, ev_flood_hazard_veno12_1]. Size and siting can reverse the effect: larger sand dams increase the risk of flooding, erosion and seepage, and check dams can cause channel incision downstream, observed at 81% of surveyed check dams in a Spanish catchment [ev_flood_hazard_ritc21_1, ev_erosion_hazard_fran21_1].

water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.mechanism: Small reservoirs store rainy-season runoff, which users perceive as limiting floods; large sand dams, however, can increase flooding, erosion and seepage risk.
water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.conditionality: Two narrative units pointing in opposite directions: a user perception from Ghana and a review statement on large sand dams; size and siting of the structure decide the outcome.

water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.mechanism: Sand dams, small reservoirs, subsurface dams and recharge structures store runoff that farmers use to irrigate more land, harvest more often and support fodder and livestock, raising crop and livestock production.
water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.conditionality: Evidence is mostly secondary or narrative (reviews citing earlier studies, an expert's personal communication on livestock, Embrapa accounts from Brazil); gains depend on an existing irrigation tradition and are uneven between sites.

water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.mechanism: Small reservoirs, sand dams, runoff cisterns and subsurface dams provide water for dry-season irrigation of vegetables and fruit and for livestock, shifting cropping towards higher-value crops and raising household income and lean-season food security.
water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.conditionality: Most magnitudes are secondary citations in reviews or vote counts; sand dams are judged likely not cost-efficient for water supply, and subsurface dams in Brazil produced little cash income where markets, electricity or irrigation experience were missing. A high benefit-cost ratio for Brazilian subsurface dams is from an upper-middle-income context.

water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.mechanism: Check dams and gabions trap sediment in gullies and channels, reducing catchment sediment export; hill reservoirs reduce outlet flows.
water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.conditionality: Check dams can cause downstream channel incision through the clear-water effect (documented in Spain, a high-income setting), and gabions fill up and need raising to keep working. The pooled sediment figures are from one synthesis, so the independent base is narrow.

water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.mechanism: Check dams and gabion structures store sediment in channels, reducing catchment sediment yield and the topsoil washed downstream.
water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.conditionality: Sediment retention is a proxy for water quality; the magnitudes come from one check-dam synthesis and gabions in Morocco have filled up and need raising to keep trapping sediment.

water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.mechanism: Sand dams, check dams, subsurface dams and production cisterns store water in sand, soil or tanks and recharge local groundwater, extending the months of water access and keeping livestock watered when other sources dry up.
water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.conditionality: The groundwater effect of sand dams is limited in space and time, many Kenyan sand dams lack capacity to supply even one household through the dry season, and only part of assessed dams would hold enough water for reported beneficiaries. Several units are review citations or vote counts rather than measurements.

water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.mechanism: Storms cause extensive damage to terraces on China's Loess Plateau, and there are few local funds to repair it [ev_climate_shock_iegchn07_7].
water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.conditionality: This is one evaluator observation with no measure of the damage; it adds that farmers' incentive to maintain terraces at their own expense may be undermined by subsidies in adjacent areas, so the threat turns as much on repair finance as on exposure [ev_climate_shock_iegchn07_7].

water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.mechanism: Banquettes lack the capacity to absorb runoff from erosive rains and overflow, diversion channels fill with eroded soil and overflow in the heaviest storms, and torrential rain collapses terrace walls or carries small terraces away in mass movements [ev_flood_hazard_heusch95_2, ev_flood_hazard_roose94_2, ev_erosion_hazard_willem21_3, ev_erosion_hazard_roose06_5].
water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.conditionality: Failure is tied to maintenance and setting: rarely maintained diversion systems generally fail after 4 to 10 years, terrace collapse is linked to abandonment, and the Rwandan mass movement happened on steep terraces without trees [ev_flood_hazard_roose94_2, ev_erosion_hazard_willem21_3, ev_erosion_hazard_roose06_5]. The hazards named are erosive rains, torrential rain and landslides mapped to flood, and the units are expert and modelled statements without failure rates [ev_flood_hazard_heusch95_2].

water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.mechanism: The single figure is the cost of rehabilitating some pre-Columbian terraces (andenes) in Peru, a heavy earth- and stone-moving intervention.
water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.conditionality: One historical assessment from an upper-middle-income Andean context, cited secondhand; it is not representative of new terrace construction in LIC/LMIC settings and carries no currency-year adjustment.

water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.mechanism: Terraces and stone bunds slow runoff and promote infiltration, raising soil moisture; when rainfall is erratic, stone bunds conserve moisture and ease crop water stress during dry spells, and crops behind stone bunds could yield two to three times more than control plots in dry years [ev_soil_water_retention_willem21_1, ev_soil_water_retention_zoug14_1, ev_crop_yield_zoug14_1_s]. Leveled fields on China's Loess Plateau increased moisture retention, broad bench terraces in semi-arid China held up to 22% more moisture than vegetated slopes, and Himachal Pradesh farmers attributed higher soil moisture to terrace repairs and vegetative field boundaries [ev_soil_water_retention_iegchn07_2, ev_soil_water_retention_willem21_2, ev_soil_water_retention_iegind11_9].
water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.conditionality: Stone bunds in Burkina Faso gave no yield benefit in the driest year and so did not reduce famine risk in a particularly dry year, which bounds the cited two-to-threefold dry-year gain [ev_crop_yield_roose94_2, ev_crop_yield_zoug14_1_s]. Narrow benches and contour-trench terraces showed no moisture advantage over vegetated slopes, the Loess Plateau result has no control, and the Indian result is farmer perception [ev_soil_water_retention_willem21_2, ev_soil_water_retention_iegchn07_2, ev_soil_water_retention_iegind11_9]. The Rwandan finding of greater resilience and faster recovery after the 2016 drought comes from a bundled land-husbandry package whose terrace share is unknown, and the remaining units measure soil moisture as a component proxy [ev_drought_hazard_rwa18_6].

water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.mechanism: Households in a terracing-centred land husbandry project were more resilient to drought and recovered faster than comparison households.
water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.conditionality: One independent DIME impact evaluation in Rwanda, reported through the World Bank completion report without a magnitude or outcome metric; the project bundled terracing with other land husbandry and irrigation investments.

water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.mechanism: The source reasons that on intensively tended terraces, where all crop residues are grazed off as soon as harvests end, fire finds no fuel, so terraces can act as a firebreak [ev_fire_hazard_roose06_1].
water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.conditionality: This is an expert estimate that the authors state has no experimental basis on terraces, and it depends on residues being removed by grazing; grass strips may instead carry fire if they are not grazed [ev_fire_hazard_roose06_1].

water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.mechanism: Bench and progressive terraces, contour stone bunds and banquettes slow and spread runoff on slopes: terraces cut mean runoff by 50 to 98% and flood peaks on small mountain plots, a global study of 105 cases finds terraces on average 2.5 times more effective than slopes at reducing runoff, stone bunds lower hillslope peak discharges, and a combined treatment in a semi-arid Tunisian catchment clipped peak discharges and cut runoff volume by 50% [ev_runoff_reduction_roose06_1, ev_flood_hazard_roose06_1, ev_runoff_reduction_willem21_1, ev_erosion_hazard_roose94_1, ev_runoff_reduction_roose06_2]. Compacted hill terraces with retention walls in Uttarakhand are credited with limiting damage from landslides and flood [ev_flood_hazard_utk22_7].
water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.conditionality: Diversion banquettes and ditches, filed in this family, do the opposite: in Niger they doubled the runoff coefficient, raised peak discharges and increased gully and bank erosion, and ditches with a downslope bank accelerate runoff and concentration time [ev_runoff_reduction_heusch95_1, ev_flood_hazard_heusch95_1, ev_erosion_hazard_heusch95_1, ev_erosion_hazard_roose06_3, ev_flood_hazard_roose94_3]. Abandoned terraces increase erosion, many Maghreb banquettes were erased or never maintained, catchment-level peak-flow evidence is scarce, and most units measure runoff or soil loss as proxies for flood impact [ev_erosion_hazard_willem21_2, ev_erosion_hazard_roose06_4, ev_flood_hazard_willem21_1]. The Rwanda sediment figures and the Uttarakhand claim are Bank self-reports, and the Tunisian result bundles rangeland closure and gully stone-filling with the bunds [ev_erosion_hazard_rwa18_1_s, ev_flood_hazard_utk22_7, ev_runoff_reduction_roose06_2].

water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.mechanism: Bench and progressive terraces and contour stone bunds detain and spread runoff on slopes, cutting peak discharge, delaying flood rise and extending flow duration; in a semi-arid Tunisian catchment a combined stone-bund treatment clipped peak discharges and halved runoff volume across 71 single-peak floods [ev_flood_hazard_roose06_1, ev_flood_hazard_roose94_1, ev_flood_hazard_roose06_2_s].
water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.conditionality: Diversion banquettes in Niger and runoff-diversion dikes raised peak discharges, and breached dikes can cause gullying, so design decides the sign [ev_flood_hazard_heusch95_1, ev_flood_hazard_roose94_3]. Catchment-scale evidence is limited, the Tunisian treatment also included rangeland closure and gully stone-filling, and the Uttarakhand flood-mitigation claim is a lender self-reported narrative [ev_flood_hazard_willem21_1, ev_flood_hazard_roose06_2_s, ev_flood_hazard_utk22_7].

water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.mechanism: Terraces, fanya juu and contour stone bunds or banquettes level slopes and slow runoff, so more water and soil stay on the field; yields of maize, barley, millet and sorghum rose on terraced or bunded land, especially in dry years, and the value of harvests rose in a terracing project. Stone bunds raised sorghum yields by 33% to 55% in Burkina Faso and by about 142% with compost, and millet yields in Niger rose by more than 40% up to 15 years after the bunds were built [ev_crop_yield_zoug14_2, ev_crop_yield_zoug14_4, ev_crop_yield_zoug14_1_s].
water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.conditionality: Several figures are lender self-reports (Rwanda before/after yields, Uttarakhand with/without models bundled with crop packages); the Rwanda value-of-harvest gain is from an independent DIME evaluation, and the Burkina Faso and Niger gains are cited from earlier studies, the largest bundled with compost [ev_crop_yield_rwa18_7, ev_crop_yield_utk22_8, ev_agricultural_production_value_rwa18_3, ev_crop_yield_zoug14_4]. Diversion banquettes in Niger reduced yields, progressive terraces on poor soils in Rwanda gave no yield increase, and bench terraces need heavy fertility restoration before yields rise [ev_crop_yield_heusch95_1, ev_crop_yield_roose06_3].

water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.mechanism: Terracing raises yields and enables higher-value crops on former hillsides, which drives positive modelled returns per hectare and improved food consumption in project households; terrace investments are judged to pay off over long lifetimes.
water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.conditionality: The returns are lender crop-budget models (Rwanda, Uttarakhand), with the Rwanda ICR itself flagging an exceptional NPV; the food-security gain is an independent DIME evaluation. A review reports terraces reducing net crop income in Ethiopia, banquette profitability in Niger was close to nil, and bench-terrace returns depend on high-value crops.

water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.mechanism: Bench and progressive terraces, contour stone bunds and banquettes shorten slope length and slow runoff, so soil losses on steep plots fall sharply and sediment loads drop where terracing is widespread. Terraces cut soil losses on small mountain plots on 20 to 60% slopes from more than 200 to under 2 t/ha a year, a contour banquette in Niger divided erosion by 150 against traditional cropping, and stone bunds with compost cut total soil loss by 79% [ev_erosion_hazard_roose06_1_s, ev_erosion_hazard_heusch95_2_s, ev_erosion_hazard_zoug14_1].
water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.conditionality: Alignment decides the sign: diversion banquettes in Niger doubled runoff coefficients and increased gully erosion, while contour banquettes in the same region cut erosion; ditches with downslope banks cause rill erosion, many Maghreb banquettes were erased or unmaintained, and abandoned terraces increase erosion [ev_runoff_reduction_heusch95_1, ev_erosion_hazard_heusch95_1, ev_erosion_hazard_heusch95_2_s, ev_erosion_hazard_roose06_3, ev_erosion_hazard_roose06_4, ev_erosion_hazard_willem21_2]. The Rwanda sediment reductions are lender-monitored before/after figures without a control [ev_erosion_hazard_rwa18_1_s, ev_erosion_hazard_rwa18_2].

water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.mechanism: Terracing and retaining walls hold soil on slopes, which IEG expects to reduce siltation of downstream rivers and dam storage.
water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.conditionality: Single evaluator assertion from Morocco; the same evaluation states that no reduction in reservoir siltation was measured.

water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.mechanism: Terraces and contour ridges retain rainfall on slopes so part of it infiltrates and recharges groundwater.
water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.conditionality: The recharge figures are a modelling study (Morocco) and an estimate from the Mandara mountains (Cameroon); catchment modelling in Peru found no difference in crop water distribution with partial terracing, and abandoned or degraded terraces worsen water regulation.

water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.mechanism: Stone bunds hold runoff in the field; in wet years this can waterlog parts of the field and harm crop production, and millet behind stone bunds can suffer waterlogging when monthly rainfall exceeds 200 mm [ev_waterlogging_hazard_zoug14_1, ev_crop_yield_roose94_3].
water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.conditionality: Both are cited statements from Burkina Faso that apply only to wet years or very wet months and give no magnitude or share of field affected [ev_waterlogging_hazard_zoug14_1, ev_crop_yield_roose94_3].

water_harvesting_conservation__water_qua.mechanism: Check dams, gabions and terraces trap sediment that would otherwise reach streams and reservoirs, lowering catchment sediment export and downstream siltation.
water_harvesting_conservation__water_qua.conditionality: Water quality is inferred from sediment retention, a component proxy; nothing is measured on nutrients or water chemistry. Much of the pooled magnitude is from one check-dam synthesis, the China figure is a modelled programme total, and IEG reports no measured reduction in reservoir siltation in Morocco while gabions there have filled.

water_harvesting_conservation__water_str.mechanism: Pits, bunds, terraces, trenches and check dams increase infiltration and groundwater recharge, raising well levels and spring discharge; cisterns, sand dams and subsurface dams store water close to homes, cutting time spent fetching water and dependence on water tankers through the dry season.
water_harvesting_conservation__water_str.conditionality: Most units are narrative, perception or lender-reported (completion reports, programme authors, Embrapa), and the pooled percentages mix recharge, spring discharge and tanker-use metrics. Groundwater gains are often local and short-lived, can be wiped out by increased pumping, and year-round wells did not increase in Burkina Faso; many sand dams cannot supply a household through the dry season, domestic cisterns cover basic needs only for small households, and trenches had little effect on baseflow or infiltration.

water_harvesting_conservation__water_str.mechanism: Storage and recharge structures ease water stress in semi-arid areas: domestic and production cisterns in semi-arid Brazil give households basic drinking water, keep livestock watered when clay tanks are dry and reduce dependence on water trucks, and subsurface dams raise water levels in existing wells used when other sources dry up [ev_water_access_deficit_arsky20_1, ev_water_access_deficit_arsky20_5, ev_water_access_deficit_arsky20_4, ev_water_access_deficit_cirilo03_1]. Stone bunds, zaï and half-moons applied at watershed scale raise groundwater levels, and in Burkina Faso improved well levels are linked to runoff control and better infiltration [ev_groundwater_recharge_potential_zoug14_1, ev_groundwater_recharge_potential_kabo04_1].
water_harvesting_conservation__water_str.conditionality: Supply is bounded by storage: a 16 thousand-litre cistern gives a family of four 16.6 litres per person-day, only 19.1% of surveyed families used the cistern as their main source, and 57% of Kenyan sand dams would hold 4 months of water for their reported beneficiaries [ev_water_access_deficit_arsky20_2, ev_water_access_deficit_silva09_2, ev_water_access_deficit_neuf17_1]. In Burkina Faso the number of wells with year-round water had not increased significantly since soil and water conservation began, and most units are implementer or agency assessments, interviews or census inference from upper-middle-income Brazil rather than the low-income target [ev_groundwater_recharge_potential_kabo04_2, ev_water_access_deficit_castro22_1, ev_water_access_deficit_arsky20_4].

water_harvesting_conservation__water_str.mechanism: In semi-arid Brazil, domestic and production cisterns and subsurface dams store rain for the dry season, giving households basic drinking water, keeping livestock watered and reducing dependence on water trucks [ev_water_access_deficit_arsky20_1, ev_water_access_deficit_arsky20_5, ev_water_access_deficit_arsky20_4, ev_water_access_deficit_cirilo03_1]. A few catchment studies of trenches observe reduced quick runoff or increased aquifer recharge [ev_groundwater_recharge_potential_locat20_1].
water_harvesting_conservation__water_str.conditionality: Storage limits the benefit: a 16 thousand-litre cistern gives a family of four 16.6 litres per person-day, larger households stay dependent on water trucks, and only 19.1% of surveyed families used the cistern as their main source [ev_water_access_deficit_arsky20_2, ev_water_access_deficit_brito07_1, ev_water_access_deficit_silva09_2]. Catchment effects are weak or unproven: recharge gains cannot be generalised, trenches have little effect on baseflow and no significant effect on infiltration rates, terracing 20% of cropland made no difference in a Peruvian catchment model, and abandoned terraces can harm water regulation [ev_groundwater_recharge_potential_locat20_1, ev_water_regulation_locat20_1, ev_soil_permeability_locat20_1, ev_water_regulation_willem21_1, ev_water_regulation_willem21_2].

water_harvesting_conservation__waterlogg.mechanism: Practices that hold water in the field can backfire in wet conditions: stone bunds retain runoff and in wet years can waterlog parts of the field, millet behind stone bunds can suffer waterlogging when monthly rainfall exceeds 200 mm, and in the humid Sudanian zone of Cameroon sorghum in zaï pits yielded less than flat-cultivated fields because of frequent waterlogging and nutrient leaching [ev_waterlogging_hazard_zoug14_1, ev_crop_yield_roose94_3, ev_crop_yield_roose93_4].
water_harvesting_conservation__waterlogg.conditionality: The effect is conditional on wet years or high-rainfall zones, and no unit gives a magnitude or the share of field affected [ev_waterlogging_hazard_zoug14_1, ev_crop_yield_roose94_3]. The Burkina Faso statements are cited rather than measured, and the Cameroon observation is unpublished work cited by the authors [ev_crop_yield_roose93_4].
